A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeaCache and contain complete, readable main text, references and eight-page supplementary material. Textual and visual inspection supports reliable comparison of all sections, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original image and video generation experiments on FLUX.1-dev, HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1, with additional runtime measurements and comparisons in supplementary Sections 8–10.

after.justification: The original quantitative and qualitative experiments remain in Section 5 and the supplement, including benchmark results, ablations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same timestep-dependent SEA filter, normalization, FFT/iFFT feature transformation and accumulated-distance cache refresh procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DrawBench text-to-image generation and VBench text-to-video generation. The main and supplementary evaluations retain the same data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including TeaCache, TaylorSeer, ToCa, Delta-DiT, DiCache and MagCache, alongside the same uncached and reduced-step references.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains 200 DrawBench prompts, 944 VBench prompts, the same resolutions and frame counts, 50-step sampling, metrics and cache budgets. Supplementary experiments also retain their stated protocols.

E4.justification: The filtering ablations, DiCache adaptation and refresh-pattern analyses in Figures 8–10 are unchanged. The oracle study, runtime and compatibility analyses, and supplementary qualitative cases are also retained.

E5.justification: The shared initial seed statement in Section 5.1 and Table 5's runtime averages over 10 runs are identical. No repeated-run, uncertainty or significance-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported scores, runtime values, rankings, plotted trends and qualitative examples match, including supplementary Tables 5–13. For example, Table 1 retains SeaCache's 9.4-second latency and 26.285 PSNR at delta = 0.3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and filter construction in Sections 3–4 and the linear-MMSE derivation in supplementary Section 7 are unchanged. Equations 1–21 retain the same assumptions and reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, architecture-agnostic spectral caching and improved latency–quality trade-offs. Contribution scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 11 retains the same limitations concerning power-law spectra, stationarity, signal–noise independence and applicability of the derivation to learned latent spaces.

D1.justification: Hardware, implementation details, filter parameters, cache settings and code access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgments disclose no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 81 bibliography entries retain the same content and research positioning. Bibliography reflow does not add or remove cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgments paragraph before References, updates the arXiv version/date stamp and changes 'Table 5' to 'Tab. 5' in Section 8. Scientific prose and narrative organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgments reflow the bibliography, and supplementary spacing and column/page breaks shift. Table 13 becomes slightly narrower and Figure 11 shifts vertically; figure and table membership, captions and substantive content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and minor typographic/layout adjustments while preserving the same method, theory, experimental evidence and limitations. These edits provide no meaningful net change in scientific clarity, evidential strength or reproducibility.
